research.label: Dogs Trust: enrichment ideas for bored dogs

substitutes: No mat? Use a folded towel or an old picnic cloth.
variations: Home version: lay the mat on a balcony, doorstep or living-room floor.
No food: pack a favorite toy instead of the lick mat.
Seated version: pick a spot you can reach with a short, flat walk.
Weather version: a short hallway picnic when it is too hot or wet outside.
title: Picnic To-Go
clue: It is already packed and by the door, and you can be gone in two minutes.
reveal: A grab-and-go outing for the days when a big plan is too much. A small bag lives by the door, so a spare half hour becomes a snack outside with your dog in the time it takes to find your shoes.
objective: Pack a small go-bag once, then use it for a quick snack-and-sniff outing at the nearest comfortable spot.
instructions: Set up the bag once: a small tote with a mat, collapsible bowl, waste bags, a small water bottle and a sealed lick mat or portion of your dog's regular food. Hang it by the door.
When a spare half hour appears, grab the bag and the leash. Choose the nearest comfortable spot within ten minutes' walk: a courtyard, park corner, quiet bench or your own yard.
Check the spot is dog-welcoming under local rules, and not too hot, cold or crowded. Leash your dog and keep them close until you settle.
Lay out the mat and offer water first. Give your dog a minute to sniff around before any food appears.
Snack time: offer the dog's portion on the lick mat while you enjoy your own snack. If your dog is not interested, there is no pressure; just sit together.
Spend ten quiet minutes looking around. Notice five things you would have walked past, and let your dog watch or sniff as they choose.
Pack up, leave the spot as you found it, and restock the bag when you get home.
twist: The bag is packed before the mood strikes, so 'maybe later' becomes 'leaving in two minutes'.
completion: Counts once the mat is down and you have spent a few minutes together at the spot, even if the snack stays in the bag.
photoIdea: The packed mat with your dog's paws or nose at the edge of it, shot low, with no posing.
memoryPrompt: Where did you end up, and what did you both notice that you usually walk past?
supplies: A lick mat or small portion of regular food

reservation.note: Check local leash and dog rules; the owner must confirm any cafe or garden allows dogs before using it.

dietNotes: Use a small portion of the dog's regular food, counted in the day's meals. Ask your vet about diet. Food-free option included.
safety: Check ground, shade and temperature for your dog; offer water and head home if they pant hard or get restless.
Keep the leash on, watch for dropped food and litter, and keep unsafe human foods out of reach.
Confirm local dog rules before you settle; leave if the spot is busy.

keepsake.headline: PICNIC TO-GO
keepsake.explainer: Two minutes from door to mat

teaser: A small bag by the door and a spare half hour can change the whole afternoon.
